unanticipated_findings: A sender configured on a path the built-in health endpoints own (/healthz, /health, /readyz, /ready) is silently shadowed and can never receive a delivery. app.py:68-71 matches those paths before ever calling config.sender_by_path (app.py:73), and config.py performs no check against them. Reproduce: `config.from_mapping({'store':{'path':':memory:'},'senders':[{'id':'h','path':'/healthz','secrets':['test-secret-with-enough-entropy']}]}, environ={})` is accepted and `c.sender_by_path('/healthz').id` returns 'h', but POSTing a correctly signed delivery to /healthz returns `405 {"error":"method_not_allowed","message":"This endpoint accepts GET."}`. `webhookd check` lists the route as if it worked, so the misconfiguration is invisible until deliveries silently stop.

A sender configured with a trailing slash in `path` is completely unreachable, including at its own exact path. app.py:252-255 `_normalise_path` strips a trailing slash from the *incoming* path, but the routing table is built from the raw configured strings (config.py:182), so nothing can ever match a key ending in '/'. Reproduce with the same from_mapping harness: path='/hooks/acme/' -> POST '/hooks/acme/' returns 404, POST '/hooks/acme' returns 404; path='/hooks/acme' -> POST '/hooks/acme/' returns 202. Config validation only checks that the path *starts* with '/' (config.py:333-334), so this passes `webhookd check` and fails silently at runtime.

With `scheme = "custom"`, setting `timestamp_header` while leaving `{timestamp}` out of the template produces a replay window that is enforced against an attacker-controlled, unsigned header — i.e. no replay protection at all, with no warning. TemplateScheme validates the inverse direction only (signatures.py:202-206: template references {timestamp} but no header -> ConfigError); nothing rejects a timestamp_header that the signature does not cover. app.py:180-188 then compares that unsigned value against the clock. Reproduce: sender with scheme_options {signature_header:'X-Sig', timestamp_header:'X-Ts', template:'{body}', prefix:''}; sign body alone; POST with X-Ts = now-7200 -> `400 stale_timestamp`, then re-POST the byte-identical body and signature with X-Ts rewritten to now -> `202 Accepted`. An attacker replaying a captured request simply rewrites the header. (Where dedup falls back to the body digest a replay is still caught as a duplicate, but the timestamp window itself contributes nothing, and a sender configured with an unsigned delivery_id_header would not be covered either.)

Not a defect, but worth recording alongside the scores: the artefact ships no version control — `git log` reports 'not a git repository' and there is no .git directory — so the 'number of commits / bisectable history' measurement is zero/not applicable for this packet.
